paper.title_en: Circuit Complexity in Charged Proca Theory
paper.abstract_en: Holographic complexity conjectures relate bulk gravitational geometry to circuit complexity of boundary quantum field theory (QFT). While the research on circuit complexity for charged vector fields remain absent, in this paper we generalize our previous research on the complexity of neutral Proca fields to the case of charged vector fields. We adopt Nielsen's approach to compute the circuit complexity of ground and thermofield double (TFD) states and derive closed-form complexity expressions using the covariance matrix method. Due to the enlargement of degrees of freedom, all complexity values of charged vector fields bear an overall multiplicative factor compared with the neutral case. We identify a characteristic contribution to complexity that exists exclusively in vector theories and vanishes in scalar QFTs. For the TFD state, this contribution delays the late-time saturation of complexity and modulates both the amplitude and period of its oscillatory behavior at late times. As in scalar and neutral vector field theories, our results show that, for charged vector field theory, the late-time saturation of complexity complies with the universal holographic predictions for eternal black holes.
